summary: Egaku Mayeda (1926–2010) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji, Shoson Miyamoto, Hajime Nakamura, and Kogen Mizuno, later holding professorships at Meijo University and Aichi Gakuin University.

Egil Asprem (born 1984) works in religious studies and history and archaeology. Educated at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology and the University of Amsterdam, he held posts at NTNU (2013), UC Santa Barbara (2013), and Stockholm University (2016).

Eido Shimano (1932–2018) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Kengan Goto, Keizan Shirozō, Soen Nakagawa at Ryutaku-ji, and at the University of Hawaiʻi, later serving as abbot of the Zen Studies Society and master at New York Zendo Shobo-ji.

Eiichi Chino (1932–2002) was a linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Harushige Takatsu. He held posts at Tokyo University of Education (~1966–1973), Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1973–1995), and Wako University (~1995–2002).

Eiichi Imoto (1930–2014) specialized in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Kyoto University (~1950–1958), he served on the faculties of Osaka University of Foreign Studies (~1964–1996) and Momoyama Gakuin University (~1996–2001).

Eiichi Makino (1878–1970) worked in philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1900–1903) and later held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1903–1938), Shiraume Gakuen Junior College (~1953–1965), Kyushu University, Tohoku University, and Chuo University.
Eiichi Otani (born 1968) works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Toyo University (~1987–1991) and was attested in 2026 as dean and professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University.
Eiichi Yamaguchi is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed graduate studies at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1990), where he was also attested as a research assistant in 1991.
Eiin Yasuda (born 1938) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Ryukoku University from circa 1957 to 1961 and trained as a disciple under Gyoin Hashimoto.
Eiju Fukushima works in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and religious studies. Fukushima is attested in 2026 as a faculty member at both Otani University and the Otani Academic Society.

Eiki Hoshino (born 1943) specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. After studying at Taisho University (~1963–1969), he served as professor in the Faculty of Humanities and director at the same institution.
Eiko Okukaze is a Buddhist studies researcher who was a doctoral student at Bukkyo University (attested 2010). Okukaze was later attested as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University in 2026.

Eileen Power (1889–1940) was a historian who studied at Girton College and the University of Paris. From circa 1921 to 1940, she held posts at the London School of Economics and the University of London.

Einar Thomassen (born 1951) works in religious studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Bergen and the University of St Andrews, later holding posts at the University of Oslo and the University of Bergen.

Eisaku Okada is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (attested 2014). Okada held posts at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (2014), Kyoto University (2015), and Koyasan University (2014, 2026).
Eisei Kojima was a Buddhist studies scholar who, in 1976, was attested as a professor at Ryukoku University and as the president of Doho University.

Eishu Miyazaki (1913–1997) specialized in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Rissho University (~1933–1937) under Gyoo Kageyama, later holding posts at Minobusan University and Rissho University (~1954–1984).
Eishun Fushimi specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Fushimi studied at the University of Hamburg (attested 1998) under David P. Jackson.
Eivind Kahrs works in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He was attested at Queens' College, Cambridge in 2010, and as a council member of the Pali Text Society in 2026.
Eizan Tatsuta (1893–1979) was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied under Sokatsu Shaku and founded Ningen Zen Kyōdan.
